# `silk/tls/trust_source`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The `TrustSource` effect: where a program gets its trust anchors.

## When to use
Require [`TrustSource`](#TrustSource) in code that needs trust anchors, such as a TLS client, so that the
caller chooses where they come from. Provide `silk.tls.trust_source_memory` for anchors in memory,
or a native provider for the CA files of the system.

## Details
Each [`TrustSource.load`](#TrustSource.load) returns a new `TrustSnapshot` that the caller owns. It stays valid
after later loads and after the provider changes. No provider is installed by default.

## Errors
- `TrustSourceError` if the provider cannot load valid trust.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` fails.

## Gotchas
Loading anchors does not validate a certificate. A provider must return only the trust that it
was configured with: no hidden system roots, environment variables, or caches.

Import as `TrustSource` with `import silk.tls.trust_source { TrustSource }`.

Public declarations: 1.

<a id="TrustSource"></a>

## `TrustSource`

```silk
pub service TrustSource
```

The effect that loads a trust snapshot. It needs exclusive access to the provider.

### When to use
Require it in code that needs trust anchors, such as a TLS client, so that the caller chooses
where they come from. Provide `silk.tls.trust_source_memory` for anchors in memory, or a native
provider for the CA files of the system. No provider is installed by default.

### Gotchas
Loading anchors does not validate a certificate. A provider must return only the trust that it
was configured with: no hidden system roots, environment variables, or caches.

<a id="TrustSource.load"></a>

### Operation `load`

```silk
effect fn load(
    limits: TrustLoadLimits
  ) -> TrustSnapshot
  ! TrustSourceError | OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut TrustSource | &mut Allocator
```

Returns a new trust snapshot from the provider, within `limits`. The caller owns it. It stays
valid after later loads and after the provider changes.

#### Errors
- `TrustSourceError` if the provider cannot load valid trust.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` fails.

A failed load returns no snapshot and does not change the trust of the provider.
